purpose: This turns two equations into arrows and a parallelogram. You solve the system by comparing areas, which is exactly what Cramer's rule does. You also see why the rule breaks when the parallelogram goes flat.

stops.title: Arrows and areas
stops.text: The green arrow u and red arrow v are the columns of numbers on the left. The blue arrow w is the right side. The yellow parallelogram of u and v has area D. Nothing is dragged here. Change the numbers with the sliders.
stops.try: Make u and v point the same way and watch the yellow shape flatten.

stops.title: The six numbers
stops.text: These sliders set a, b, c, d, e, f in ax + by = e and cx + dy = f. The arrows, the area D and the equations at the top all update at once. They stay live in every step except practice.
stops.try: Change e and f only. Which arrow moves, and does D change?

stops.title: A slide that reads x
stops.text: In step 2, answer the prediction first. Then this slider is unlocked. The violet parallelogram of w and v slides along v until it sits on x copies of u. Sliding does not change its area, so x equals that area divided by D.
stops.try: Drag it back and forth. Does the area label ever change?

stops.title: Swap a column
stops.text: In step 3, choose Find x or Find y, then replace that unknown's column with the right side. The matching violet parallelogram appears and its area is the top number of the fraction.
stops.try: Pick Find x, then press Replace the x column. Compare with the y one.

stops.title: Do the arithmetic
stops.text: Set Bottom number D and Top number with the two sliders, then press this. It tells you which one is wrong and why, such as adding where you should subtract. Solve both x and y to see the walk to w.
stops.try: Check one wrong answer on purpose to read the hint.

stops.title: When D is zero
stops.text: In step 4, the parallelogram is flat. Decide between one solution, no solution or infinitely many, then read why. It depends on whether the right side w sits on the line through u and v.
stops.try: Change e and f so that w lies on the line, then choose again.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 introduces the arrows and D. Step 2 reads x from a slide. Step 3 builds the rule with the sliders. Step 4 uses a flat parallelogram with no unique answer.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: A few questions at the end. A wrong answer explains itself and you can try again.

teacher: Project step 2 and have students predict x before the slide. Then ask why sliding does not change the area (same base, same height). Common slip: students swap the wrong column, or add the cross products instead of subtracting. Step 4 shows why dividing by D = 0 fails.
